short: An English general and Parliamentary commander-in-chief during the English Civil War, leading the New Model Army to decisive victory.
full:
Thomas Fairfax, 3rd Lord Fairfax of Cameron, was a pivotal English politician and military commander during the English Civil War. Unlike many of his contemporaries, he was a professional soldier who had seen action in the Low Countries before the outbreak of domestic hostilities in 1642. When Parliament reformed its forces into the New Model Army in 1645, Fairfax was appointed as its captain-general and commander-in-chief, with Oliver Cromwell serving as his second-in-command.

Under Fairfax's leadership, the New Model Army achieved a decisive triumph over the Royalist forces of Charles I at the Battle of Naseby in June 1645, effectively breaking the king's military capability. Though a staunch Parliamentarian, Fairfax was a moderate who opposed the king's execution in 1649 and refused to participate in the show trial. He eventually resigned his commission in 1650 rather than lead a preemptive strike against Scotland. After Cromwell's death, Fairfax re-emerged to help organise the Restoration of Charles II, securing a peaceful transition before retiring to his Yorkshire estates.
